system.context: Orbit's older runbooks are long paragraphs with no headings, so the block packer has nothing to pack and ingest fell back to fixed windows of twelve words with no overlap. The recovery instruction 'set the timeout to thirty seconds' was cut in two at a window boundary: the retriever returned one chunk ending 'set the' and another beginning 'timeout to thirty seconds'.
system.request: A worked Python example of one action: chunk_words(text, window, overlap), which splits a document into windows of `window` words that start every `window - overlap` words, so the last `overlap` words of each chunk open the next one. The function splits on whitespace, walks range(0, n, stride), caps each window end with min, records each chunk as a dictionary with an id, its start and end positions, and its text, and breaks after the window that reaches the end so no redundant tail window is emitted; it raises ValueError for a window below 1 or an overlap outside 0 to window - 1 and returns no chunks for an empty document. A helper whole_in reports the chunks that contain a span whole. The lesson leads with the complete solution and its exact output over one inline paragraph of thirty-nine words (the five chunks, the storage cost, the instruction span whole in c3 and cut without overlap, the two rejected settings), explains the Python construct by construct, traces every window, and offers one practice variation: expanding a retrieval hit to its neighbouring chunks.
inputs: One document written inline in solution.py: a thirty-nine word runbook paragraph of four sentences, with WINDOW 12, OVERLAP 4, and SPAN (22, 28) for the instruction 'set the timeout to thirty seconds,'
For the practice variation, SENTENCE (20, 32) for the twelve-word recovery sentence and HIT 'c3', the chunk a retriever returned
outputs: chunk_words returns five chunks at word positions 0-12, 8-20, 16-28, 24-36, and 32-39 with ids c1 to c5 and their texts; 55 words are stored for 39 (1.41x); whole_in finds the instruction whole in c3 and in no chunk when the overlap is 0

python solution.py prints the five chunks, the storage line, the span checks with overlap 4 and 0, the two rejected settings, and OK; python/fixtures/expected-output.txt holds that output byte for byte

python starter.py prints NOT OK and exits 1 as shipped; after the practice change a hit on c3 expands to c2, c3, c4 (words 8 to 35), which contains the whole sentence, and c1 and c5 expand to two chunks each, as python/fixtures/expected-practice-output.txt records for practice_answer.py
constraints: Standard library only; each lesson file runs alone in an empty directory with python -I -S; no fixtures, credentials, or network

Windows advance by exactly window - overlap words; every chunk has at most window words; neighbouring chunks share exactly overlap words; every word is in at least one chunk; no chunk lies inside another; the input string is never modified
A window below 1 or an overlap outside 0 to window - 1 raises ValueError with a message naming the setting; an empty or blank document returns an empty list

Ordinary Python only: str.split, range with a step, min, slicing, join, f-strings, a list of dictionaries, break, star-unpacking of a tuple argument, and the `or` default for an empty join; no classes, regular expressions, or comprehensions in the lesson files
successCriteria: solution.py run alone exits 0 and its output equals expected-output.txt byte for byte: the five chunk rows, 55 words stored for 39 (1.41x), the instruction whole in c3, whole in none with overlap 0 and the boundary at word 24, the two rejected lines, and OK

The window arithmetic holds under a brute-force check: every span of up to overlap + 1 words is whole in some chunk at every position, for several window and overlap settings, and no longer length has that guarantee

starter.py run alone exits 1 with NOT OK and no traceback; practice_answer.py run alone exits 0 and matches expected-practice-output.txt, with the expansion clamped at both ends of the chunk list and an unknown id rejected

What shipped is measured on the same document: overlap 0 ends one chunk with 'set the' and starts the next with 'timeout to thirty seconds,', stores 39 words against 55, and guarantees only single words a home

checks.description: solution.py copied alone into an empty directory and run with python -I -S exits 0 with empty stderr and prints expected-output.txt byte for byte.
The five chunks sit at 0-12, 8-20, 16-28, 24-36, and 32-39 with ids c1 to c5, and each text is the join of its word slice.
Every chunk has at most twelve words, and neighbouring chunks start eight words apart and share exactly four words.
Every word position is covered, no chunk lies inside another, and the loop stops at five chunks instead of emitting a sixth that would only repeat words.

By brute force over every position and length, the longest span length that is always whole in some chunk is overlap + 1, for the lesson's settings and for several others; the six-word instruction fits by position and the twelve-word sentence fits nowhere.

A window of 0, an overlap equal to the window, and a negative overlap raise ValueError naming the setting; an empty or blank document returns no chunks; a short document is one chunk; window 2 with overlap 1 steps one word at a time.
Splitting the document on whitespace and joining with single spaces gives the document back, with thirty-nine words and the instruction at positions 22 to 27.
starter.py run alone exits 1, starts with the NOT OK line about the expansion of c3, and writes no traceback.
practice_answer.py run alone exits 0 and prints expected-practice-output.txt byte for byte.
expand on c3 returns c2, c3, c4 at words 8 to 35 containing the whole recovery sentence; c1 and c5 expand to two chunks; an unknown id raises ValueError.
The practice answer differs from the starter only inside its marked answer region: the data above and the demonstration below are identical text.
document.json equals the paragraph, window, overlap, span, sentence, and hit that the lesson files define.

expected-trace.json equals the trace derived from the real functions: the five chunks, 55 words stored (1.410256x), the span whole in c3 and in no flat chunk with the boundary at 24, and the expansion c2, c3, c4 at words 8 to 36.

With overlap 0 the windows sit at 0-12, 12-24, 24-36, 36-39, the instruction is whole in none, one chunk ends 'set the' and the next begins 'timeout to thirty seconds,'; with overlap 4 it is whole in c3.
Overlap 4 stores 55 words in five chunks against 39 words in four chunks without overlap: 1.41 times the text to embed and store.
Overlap 4 keeps every span of up to five words whole somewhere; overlap 0 guarantees only single words.
